per_theorem_calls.label: Theorem 1: constructive same-size rounding upper bound

published_prior_art.cite: EmamiPass2024 establishes a non-Monge barycentric discrete quadratic example; Haus2015 treats bottleneck mixability rather than this average signed-quadratic fractional-to-row loss.
Friesecke2019 gives a distinct symmetric finite-polytope non-Monge construction, not an all-N bounded signed-scalar exact 1/N loss family.
GaoGeQian2025 characterizes the unrestricted fractional causal MOT set; EmamiPass2024 and Haus2015 do not give this same-marginal average-cost frontier.
AronowGreenLee2014: sharp two-arm variance bounds from comonotone/countermonotone quantile couplings.
GaoGeQian2025 supplies the fractional causal MOT target and BrennanEtAl2025 supplies numerical integer-program copula completion, neither the claimed universal analytic same-N certificate width.
AronowGreenLee2014 gives two-arm sharp-bound plug-ins and GaoGeQian2025 analyzes fractional MOT plug-ins; the three-arm realizable-endpoint layer is distinct but builds on both.
PuccettiWang2015 and Haus2015 cover rearrangement/mixability geometry but do not determine this normalized fractional-to-realizable squared-cost constant.

soundness_flags.label: thm:plugin-endpoints, final coverage interval
soundness_flags.one_line: The asserted finite-sample coverage radius drops the deterministic realization residual: the preceding bound is [D_N(F,G)+3456/N]/(N-1), so Markov on D_N yields a radius [M_N/eta+3456/N]/(N-1), not M_N/[eta(N-1)].

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and bibliographic record, lines 8-16 and 21-32
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proceedings paper casts causal partial identification as K-marginal MOT, obtains the exact partial identified set, and gives plug-in l2-cost convergence/minimax results for arbitrary K and d<=4.

source_verification_receipts.version: Operations Research Forum 6, article 46, version of record, 7 April 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives a three-marginal, three-support-point, two-dimensional quadratic barycentric non-Monge example and states its two-marginal and one-dimensional Monge boundary cases.

The paper studies complete mixability and multidimensional bottleneck assignment, reports NP-hardness/strong complexity results, and gives fixed-dimension approximation results for the bottleneck objective.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Primary landing page; full-text iframe inaccessible; claim-level corroboration from arXiv:1405.6555
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited article is the published sharp-bounds paper for completely randomized two-arm experiments; its accessible author version describes sharp marginal-compatible variance bounds and their plug-in interval estimator.

source_verification_receipts.version: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proposes an integer program for a worst-case copula in generalized causal bootstrap settings and proves asymptotic validity across several assignment mechanisms and estimator classes.
The paper proves a finite three-marginal, three-site symmetric-pairwise-cost non-Monge counterexample and analyzes the associated Kantorovich-polytope extreme points.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 112(520), 1759-1769, 2017
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article treats finite-population randomization-based causal inference, with fixed finite populations and treatment assignment as the randomness, including multiple-treatment-level designs.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct the final plug-in coverage interval to include the deterministic term 3456/[N(N-1)] (or prove a sharper data-dependent deterministic width and use that instead).

Add a small exact worked instance reporting V_rel, the rounded schedule, C_alg, V_int, and the actual certificate width; this would make the constructive claim auditable beyond the loose universal constant.

Develop a fixed-K or contrast-geometry extension with explicit K and norm dependence, while proving where the three-arm hierarchy ceases to extend; that would materially broaden the mathematical frontier.

recommended_next_step: Revise the finite-sample coverage statement to retain the deterministic rounding residual, then advance this field-tier kernel to Stage 0.
